true_positives.golden_comment: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
The new `downsize` definition breaks the existing dimensions API

Ruby does not overload methods by arity: this definition replaces the preceding `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` definition. Existing callers that pass separate width and height values will now pass the height as `opts` or raise an argument error, breaking downsizing. Retain support for the old call signature while accepting the new geometry-string form.

true_positives.golden_comment: Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Configured attachment size limits are ignored

This replaces the per-type `max_image_size_kb` / `max_attachment_size_kb` limits with a fixed 10 MB limit. Attachments are not downsized, so sites that allow attachments larger than 10 MB will now reject them in the browser even though the server is configured to accept them. Preserve the configured attachment limit and apply any fixed cap only where intended.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.
The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.

false_positives.candidate:
Downsizing can discard animated GIF frames

When `allow_animated_thumbnails` is false, `OptimizedImage.optimize` selects the non-animated downsize instructions, which read only `from[0]`. Because this call overwrites the uploaded file, an oversized animated GIF is reduced to its first frame and loses its animation. Thumbnail animation preferences should not cause destructive changes to the uploaded original.

true_positives.golden_comment: Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Legacy host values are inserted without normalization

The old allowlist accepted host entries containing a scheme or path, but this migration copies each entry verbatim. `record_for_host` later compares the stored value to `URI(...).host`, which contains only the hostname, so migrated entries such as `https://example.com/path` will never match and those sites will lose embed access after upgrade.

true_positives.golden_comment: The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Migration crashes when no embed category is configured

The category lookup assumes the query returns a row, then dereferences `[0]['id']`. If `embed_category` is unset, its value does not match any category (or the setting row is absent), so the migration raises before it can finish. This is a normal configuration and will prevent the upgrade from completing.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

false_positives.candidate:
Configured hosts with ports can never match

The model validation accepts hosts such as `example.com:8080`, and the normalization callback preserves the port. However, `URI(host).host` returns only `example.com`, so this query compares the stored `example.com:8080` against `example.com` and rejects the referer. Any allowed host configured with a port therefore cannot embed.

SELECT row count is checked with cmd_tuples

`cmd_tuples` reports rows affected by commands such as INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE; for a SELECT it is typically zero. Consequently, even when the legacy `embeddable_hosts` setting contains hosts, this condition skips the inserts, and line 31 then deletes the old settings. The upgrade silently loses the allowlist and leaves embedding disabled.

true_positives.golden_comment: logic: Potential nil pointer exception - if no TopicUser record exists, tu will be nil and calling methods on it will crash
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Unsubscribe crashes when the user has no topic-user row

`find_by` can return nil for a recipient who has never visited or otherwise created a `TopicUser` row for this topic; such users can still receive mention or reply notification emails. The following access to `tu.notification_level` then raises a `NoMethodError`, so the unsubscribe link fails for them. Create or update the row through `TopicUser.change` instead of assuming it exists.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Typo in property name: 'stopNotificiationsText' should be 'stopNotificationsText' (missing 'n' in 'Notifications')

false_positives.candidate:
A GET unsubscribe link toggles state on every visit

This action is exposed only as GET, but it mutates the user's notification setting, and the operation toggles between muted and regular. Reopening or refreshing the email link can therefore undo the unsubscribe and resume notifications. Make the operation idempotently set muted, and avoid changing notification state on a GET request.

Unsubscribe does not mute watched or tracked topics

When the user is watching or tracking this topic, this branch changes the level to `regular`, not `muted`. Regular topics can still generate direct reply and mention notifications, so the email link's promise to stop notifications is not met for these users. Set the level to muted for this unsubscribe action.

true_positives.golden_comment: BlockedEmail.should_block_email? method has side effects during a read operation - it updates statistics even when just checking if an email should be blocked. This could cause race conditions in concurrent environments and makes the method name misleading.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Concurrent matches can lose counter increments

The method reads `match_count`, increments the in-memory value, and saves it. If two signup validations match the same blocked address concurrently, both can read the same count and write the same incremented value, losing one match. Use an atomic database increment so the match statistics remain accurate under concurrent attempts.

true_positives.golden_comment: The case-sensitive email lookup in `BlockedEmail.should_block?` creates a bypass risk, allowing 'User@Example.com' to bypass a block on 'user@example.com'. This can lead to unauthorized access to blocked users.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Blocked-email lookup is case-sensitive

This query compares the submitted address exactly with the stored address. User signup assigns the submitted email without normalizing it, so an address such as `BLOCK@SPAMMERS.ORG` can bypass a block entry stored as `block@spammers.org`. Normalize addresses consistently or make the lookup case-insensitive so casing cannot evade the block.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The regex pattern @(#{domains}) in email_in_restriction_setting? method only matches domain suffixes, not full domains with proper boundary anchoring. An attacker can register evil.example.com to bypass a whitelist entry for example.com.

true_positives.golden_comment: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Standard RSS items without a content field abort feed polling

RSS items commonly provide their body in `description` rather than `content`; when `i.content` is nil, calling `scrub` raises and aborts the polling job. Since retries are disabled, the feed is not imported on that run, including any later items. Fall back to the available description/content field and handle items with no body.

true_positives.golden_comment: An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
The Referer is interpolated unescaped into executable JavaScript

`request.referer` is inserted directly into a single-quoted JavaScript string. A referring page on the configured embeddable host can use a URL containing JavaScript-breaking characters to inject code that executes in the forum's origin when the embed loads. Serialize the value as a safely escaped JavaScript string and pass only a validated origin to `postMessage`.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

false_positives.candidate:
Imported feed HTML bypasses post sanitization

This creates imported posts with `raw_html`, and `Post#cook` returns that raw value without passing it through the normal sanitization/rendering pipeline. RSS/Atom item content is external and can contain executable markup such as `<script>` or event-handler attributes, so importing a malicious feed can give every reader of the topic stored XSS. Sanitize feed content with an explicit allowlist before storing it as raw HTML, or use the normal cooking pipeline.

Post-processing jobs can run before the imported topic transaction commits

`PostCreator#create` enqueues post-processing jobs before this surrounding `Topic.transaction` commits. A worker on another connection can run immediately, fail to find the uncommitted post, and leave imported content unprocessed. Defer job enqueueing until after the outer transaction commits, or otherwise ensure the worker cannot run before commit.

Remote article retrieval can follow redirects to internal services

The embed URL's hostname is checked against the configured host before retrieval, but `open(url)` follows HTTP redirects without revalidating the destination. A URL on the allowed host that redirects to an internal address can therefore make the application server fetch internal resources; the URL's port is also unrestricted. Validate every redirect destination and restrict schemes, ports, and private-network addresses before fetching.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.
-ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
-webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.

false_positives.candidate:
Flex layout disables the action button's right float

Making `.small-action` a flex container turns its direct children into flex items, and `float: right` on the button no longer positions it at the right edge. Since `.small-action-desc` also has no flex-grow or other rule to consume the remaining space, the button will sit immediately after the description instead of remaining right-aligned as before. Give the description a growing flex value or push the button with `margin-left: auto`.

true_positives.golden_comment: The include_website_name method is missing the required ? suffix. Rails serializers expect include_ methods to end with ? for conditional attribute inclusion, a convention followed by other methods in this serializer. Without it, the website_name attribute may not be conditionally included as intended. Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Website name bypasses the untrusted-website filter

`website` is explicitly filtered by `untrusted_attributes` for TL0 users viewed by anonymous users, but the newly serialized `website_name` has no `include_website_name?` guard and is not included in that filter. Its value is derived from the same website URL, so anonymous responses still reveal the website host and, for matching domains, its path even when the website is supposed to be hidden.

false_positives.candidate:
Sibling-domain matching mistakes shared public suffixes for the same domain

This comparison treats any two hosts with the same number of labels and the same labels after the first as belonging to the same domain. For example, with the instance at `forum.example.co.uk` and a user's website at `other.co.uk`, both hosts have three labels and the compared suffixes are both `co.uk`; the serializer incorrectly appends the website path. This produces the complete-path display for unrelated domains, contrary to the same-domain behavior this change is intended to provide.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.
The remove_member test uses xhr :put to call the remove_member action, but the route defines delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member' requiring DELETE method.
Expected to return a value at the end of function - code paths without explicit returns will return undefined

The route provides the group's ID in params[:id], but the code attempts to read it from params[:group_id], causing the action to fail. This results in a broken feature when trying to access group memberships.

Group creation ignores the selected alias level

The admin form sends `alias_level` when creating a group, but this action only assigns `name` and `visible` before saving. A newly created group therefore keeps the model default alias level regardless of the value selected in the form.

Pass a user record when deleting through the association

`group.users.delete` expects associated user records, but this passes the integer `user_id`. Active Record can reject the integer as the wrong association type, causing the remove-member request to fail instead of removing the membership. Load the user or delete the matching association row by ID.

Public group member pages now return only the first 50 members

Consider normalizing the input locale (e.g., to a symbol) when checking/loading here to avoid double-loading if the same locale is passed as a String vs Symbol (also applies to other locations in the PR).

false_positives.candidate:
Changing the site default locale leaves cached fallback results stale

The fallback chain depends on the runtime `SiteSetting.default_locale`, but the translation cache is keyed only by translation key, active locale, and backend. If the site default locale changes, cached translations for keys missing in the active locale continue returning the old fallback translation until the cache is evicted or cleared, even though lookups should now use the new default.

Fallback locales are loaded only for controller requests

This is the only call that loads the configured fallback chain. `translate_accelerator.rb` loads only the active locale when `I18n.t` is called, so translations performed outside an `ApplicationController` request—such as in background jobs or standalone mailer execution—can try the site-default/English fallback without those locale files loaded and incorrectly return a missing translation.

Do not gate conditional passkeys on an identified user

This helper is used to decide whether to call `fillContextForm` both when initially rendering the login form and when re-rendering it after an error. true_positives.golden_comment: The OptimizedCursorPaginator in organization_auditlogs.py attempts to use negative slice offsets on Django querysets, but Django querysets do not support negative slicing and will raise an AssertionError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Negative cursor offsets still raise on QuerySet slicing

This branch passes a negative start index to a Django `QuerySet` slice. Django does not support negative QuerySet indices and raises `ValueError` (“Negative indexing is not supported”), so an optimized-pagination request with a negative cursor offset produces an error rather than supporting the advertised reverse pagination. `Cursor.from_string()` accepts negative offsets, making this reachable with a cursor supplied by the client.

true_positives.golden_comment: get_item_key assumes a numeric key, but the paginator is used with order_by=-datetime in the audit logs endpoint; calling math.floor/ceil on a datetime will raise a TypeError.

Optimized paginator cannot paginate datetime fields

This paginator is selected by the audit-log endpoint with `order_by="-datetime"`, but its key handling is copied from the numeric `Paginator`: `math.floor()`/`math.ceil()` cannot accept a `datetime`. On the first non-empty page, `build_cursor()` calls this method and raises `TypeError`, so requests using optimized pagination fail instead of returning audit logs. It also needs the datetime-to-cursor conversion and reverse conversion used by `DateTimePaginator`.

Optimized pagination fails for datetime sort keys

false_positives.candidate:
The set-to-sorted-set change breaks existing live buffer keys

Before this deployment, span payloads are stored in Redis sets; this code now calls `ZADD` on the same key names, and the Lua script also uses sorted-set commands on those keys. Existing keys will remain sets until their TTL expires, so during a rollout any new span that touches one will fail with Redis `WRONGTYPE` and its batch will not be processed. Use versioned keys or provide a migration/compatibility path before switching the data type.

false_negatives.golden_comment: In _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling(), the check `if client_sample_rate:` treats 0.0 as falsy, so a sample_rate of 0.0 is silently skipped and never set on normalized_data.

Using Python’s built-in hash() to build cache keys is non-deterministic across processes (hash randomization), so keys won’t match across workers and invalidate_upsampling_cache may fail to delete them. Use a deterministic serialization of project_ids for the cache key.

The upsampling eligibility check passes the outer dataset instead of the actual dataset used by scoped_dataset. In paths where the query ultimately runs against discover (e.g., dashboard split) while the original dataset is metrics, upsampling may be skipped even when all projects are allowlisted.

false_positives.candidate:
Substring matching enables upsampling for negated error filters

This check treats any query containing `event.type:error` as an error-only query, including negated filters such as `!event.type:error` and mixed OR expressions. Those queries can include transactions or other non-error events, for which `sample_weight` is not available; replacing `count()` with `sum(sample_weight)` can therefore fail or return incorrect counts. Determine the event types from the parsed query semantics rather than a substring.

The errors dataset emits a function registered only for discover

The eligibility check explicitly enables this transformation for the `errors` dataset, so this code emits `upsampled_count()` for errors-dataset queries. The function is registered in the discover dataset's function converter, not the errors dataset's converter; an errors-dataset request can therefore fail query parsing with an unknown-function error. Register the function for that dataset too, or avoid transforming queries whose dataset does not support it.

true_positives.golden_comment: Using zip(error_ids, events.values()) assumes the get_multi result preserves the input order; dict value order is not guaranteed to match error_ids, so event data can be paired with the wrong ID (missing nodes also shift alignment).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Error details can be associated with the wrong event ID

`get_multi` returns results keyed by node ID, but this zips the original IDs with the mapping's values, relying on positional order and on missing nodes being retained. If a requested node is missing, or the mapping order differs from the request order, an event's details are labeled with another event's ID. This can place errors at the wrong timestamp and send mismatched error context to the replay summarizer; associate each result with its node ID explicitly.

true_positives.golden_comment: Validation logic incorrectly uses .get('timestamp'), which treats a timestamp of 0 as absent. Age/timestamp validation accepts invalid combinations

The serializer also accepts reports containing neither field, although the supported report formats require one of them. Use presence-based cross-field validation and require exactly one format field so malformed reports are rejected.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The BrowserReportingCollectorEndpoint returns HttpResponse objects but the endpoint inherits from Endpoint which expects rest_framework.response.Response objects.

Analytics events are recorded before the feature flag check, resulting in analytics being logged for all requests, including those that return 404 due to the feature being disabled. This can lead to misleading analytics data.

true_positives.golden_comment: Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Backup-code consumption is vulnerable to concurrent replay

This read-modify-write sequence is not atomic: two login requests can both read the same stored code, both find it, and both authenticate before either update is visible. Concurrent use of different codes can also overwrite one another and restore a code that was already consumed. Since backup codes are promised to work exactly once, consume them with an atomic conditional update or transaction/lock so only one request can succeed.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The exported function TwoFactor handles backup codes and is in BackupCode.tsx. Inconsistent naming.
Error message mentions 'backup code login' but this is a disable endpoint, not login

Backup code validation is case-sensitive due to the use of indexOf(). This causes validation to fail if a user enters uppercase hex characters, as backup codes should be case-insensitive for a better user experience.

Object URL for backup codes is not revoked on component unmount, leading to a potential memory leak. This can cause increased memory usage over time, especially if the component is mounted and unmounted frequently.

false_positives.candidate:
The external-provider 2FA flow does not offer backup-code recovery

When OAuth or SAML login redirects to the `totpEmail` flow, this conditional renders `ExternalTotpFooter` instead of `TwoFactorFooter`, so users never see the new “Lost access” option or a backup-code input. This can affect users whose account has 2FA enabled when its identity provider changes; even if the UI offered recovery, `authorize` also rejects a non-CAL user's request without `totpCode` before reaching the backup-code branch. Such users cannot use their backup codes to sign in.

true_positives.golden_comment: A null reference occurs in GoogleCalendarService.createEvent() and updateEvent() when mainHostDestinationCalendar is destructured from evt.destinationCalendar but evt.destinationCalendar is null or an empty array, causing mainHostDestinationCalendar to be undefined.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Meet bookings crash when no destination calendar is configured

When `evt.destinationCalendar` is null or empty, destructuring leaves `mainHostDestinationCalendar` undefined, and this condition dereferences `.integration`. Creating an event with Google Meet and no destination calendar therefore throws before calendar or meeting events can be created; the previous optional-chain check handled this case.

true_positives.golden_comment: Logic error: when externalCalendarId is provided, you're searching for a calendar where externalId === externalCalendarId, but this will always fail since you're looking for a calendar that matches itself. Should likely find by credentialId or use different logic.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Google update cannot fall back to the configured destination calendar

When `externalCalendarId` is absent, this lookup searches for a destination whose `externalId` equals that absent value, so it cannot select a configured destination calendar. `calendarId` is then undefined and Google event updates fail, even though the event contains the destination calendar. The analogous lookup in `deleteEvent` also falls through to `primary`, which can leave the event in its actual destination calendar.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The Calendar interface now requires createEvent(event, credentialId), but some implementations (e.g., Lark/Office365) still declare createEvent(event) only—this breaks the interface contract (also applies to other locations in the PR).
The optional chaining on mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration is redundant since you already check mainHostDestinationCalendar in the ternary condition.

Logic inversion in organization creation: The slug property is now conditionally set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, instead of when it's false as originally intended. This change, combined with requestedSlug still being set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, results in both properties being set when billing is enabled, and neither when disabled

The `credential` may be undefined when passed to `updateEvent` if `reference.credentialId` is set but the credential is not found. This can lead to a runtime error when `updateEvent` is called with an undefined credential, which should be handled to prevent crashes.

false_positives.candidate:
Recurring cancellation does not delete events for every calendar reference

For recurring bookings, this loop iterates the organizer's credentials and then selects only the first calendar reference for each updated booking. It does not use the current reference being processed or match each booking reference to its credential. With multiple host calendar references, cancellation can repeatedly target the first calendar and leave the other hosts' recurring events behind.

Rescheduling a multi-calendar booking deletes only one old calendar event

This change collects and updates all calendar references, but the old-event cleanup below still uses `booking.references.find(...)` and deletes only the first calendar reference. When a booking has multiple host calendar events, rescheduling with `newBookingId` leaves the remaining old events on their calendars as stale duplicates.

true_positives.golden_comment: The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
The minimum schema strips refreshed token fields

This computed key is a literal property name, not a wildcard for numeric expiry fields. Zod objects also strip unrecognized keys by default, so parsing a synced response retains only `access_token` and discards expiry and other provider fields. Callers then persist incomplete credentials; for example, Zoom assigns the missing `refresh_token` from the parsed response and can no longer refresh again, while Office 365 does not receive a new expiry. Preserve the response fields and explicitly extract the expiry value.

true_positives.golden_comment: When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
The sync path returns a Fetch Response instead of the provider's token response

When credential syncing is enabled, this returns the raw `fetch` `Response`, while the fallback returns each provider's native response shape. Callers are written for those native shapes: Google reads `res.data`, Bigin and Zoho CRM read `tokenInfo.data`, and HubSpot reads token fields directly. Those accesses fail or produce undefined token fields in sync mode, so refreshes break for these integrations. Normalize the sync response to the shape each caller expects, or update callers to parse the response consistently.

true_positives.golden_comment: When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

When credential syncing is enabled, this returns the raw `fetch` `Response`, while the fallback returns each provider's native response shape. true_positives.golden_comment: The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Bigin sends the credential ID as the Cal.com user ID

The third argument is used by `refreshOAuthTokens` as `calcomUserId`, but this call passes `credentialId`, which is the credential row's database ID. A sync endpoint that looks up credentials by Cal.com user ID will look up the wrong user and cannot refresh this credential. Pass the owning user's ID instead.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Salesforce client is initialized with the pre-refresh access token

The refresh response is saved to the credential, but the connection below is constructed using `credentialKey.access_token`, which is the token loaded before the refresh. When that token has expired, the current operation still uses the expired token and fails even though a new token was successfully obtained. Initialize the connection with `accessTokenParsed.data.access_token`.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

false_positives.candidate:
Salesforce token refresh bypasses credential syncing

This refresh request still calls Salesforce directly rather than using `refreshOAuthTokens`. With credential syncing configured, Salesforce credentials therefore continue to refresh against Cal.com's app credentials instead of the self-hosted source of truth, so the feature does not work for Salesforce.

true_positives.golden_comment: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Blacklist checks can be bypassed by changing email case

The blacklist entries are lowercased, but `guest` is compared without normalization. Email addresses are case-insensitive for delivery, so a blacklisted address submitted with uppercase letters bypasses this check and is added and emailed. Normalize the submitted address before checking the blacklist.

true_positives.golden_comment: The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Team admins and owners are incorrectly required to hold both roles

This uses `&&` between the admin and owner checks, so a user must be both a team admin and a team owner to pass this authorization branch. Admin-only and owner-only users are denied even though the booking UI treats admins or owners as authorized. Use an OR condition so the API matches the intended permission.

true_positives.golden_comment: The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Email notifications use the unfiltered guest list

`guests` can include addresses already attending the booking, but those addresses are removed from `uniqueGuests` before insertion. Passing the original list to `sendAddGuestsEmails` makes the email code treat those existing attendees as newly added and send them a normal scheduled-booking email when the request also includes a genuinely new guest. Pass the filtered list instead.

false_negatives.golden_comment: uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.

The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.

false_positives.candidate:
Calendar update failures leave attendee records committed without notifications

Attendee records are committed at line 92 before this external calendar update. If the calendar provider call throws, the mutation fails and execution never reaches the email send, but the guests remain in the database; retrying with those guests can then fail as duplicates. Handle this failure consistently, for example by rolling back the write or recording a retryable calendar/email job.

Guests can be added to bookings that are no longer active

The handler updates attendees without checking the booking status. A direct API call can add guests to a cancelled or rejected booking, after which the handler sends confirmed calendar invitations for that event. Reject bookings whose status does not permit adding guests before writing attendee records.

true_positives.golden_comment: Using retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 reads a possibly stale value and can lose increments under concurrency; consider an atomic increment via Prisma (increment: 1) to avoid race conditions (also applies to the similar update in the catch block).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Concurrent failures can lose retry-count increments

This writes an absolute value derived from the count read earlier, rather than incrementing the database value atomically. If overlapping cron invocations process the same reminder and both read the same `retryCount`, both can write the same next value; repeated overlaps can prevent the count from reaching 2, leaving failed reminders eligible for retries indefinitely. Use an atomic increment (and coordinate processing if concurrent sends must also be prevented).

false_negatives.golden_comment: The deletion logic in scheduleSMSReminders.ts incorrectly deletes non-SMS workflow reminders (e.g., Email, WhatsApp) that have retryCount > 1. This occurs because the retryCount condition within the OR clause for deletion lacks a method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, causing it to apply to all reminder types instead of only SMS reminders, which is the intended scope of this function.

false_positives.candidate:
Reminders without a recipient or message never reach the retry limit

When `sendTo` is empty or `message` is empty, this condition skips scheduling without incrementing `retryCount` or otherwise removing the reminder. The cron job will select the same unscheduled reminder on every run, so these unprocessable reminders are never cleaned up despite the retry limit.

false_negatives.golden_comment: In getBaseConditions(), the else if (filterConditions) and final else branches are unreachable. This is because getAuthorizationConditions() always returns a non-null Prisma.Sql object, making authConditions always truthy, which means only the first two if/else if conditions are ever evaluated.

Fetching userIdsFromOrg only when teamsFromOrg.length > 0 can exclude org-level members for orgs without child teams; consider deriving from teamIds (which includes orgId) or removing the guard so org-only orgs still include member user bookings.

false_positives.candidate:
Removing `findMany` breaks existing service callers

This change removes the public `findMany` method and replaces it with `getBaseConditions`, but the PR does not update any callers. Existing code that calls `InsightsBookingService.findMany(...)` will fail to compile or, if reached dynamically, fail at runtime. Preserve the method with an appropriate raw-query implementation or migrate all callers in this change.

true_positives.golden_comment: logic: macOS-specific sed syntax with empty string after -i flag will fail on Linux systems
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Use a sed in-place-edit form that works on Linux

`sed -i ''` is the BSD/macOS form for an in-place edit and fails with GNU sed, commonly used in Linux development and CI environments. When `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL` already exists, the script therefore cannot update the env file on those systems. Use a portable edit strategy or branch for the platform.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The updateManyByCredentialId call uses an empty data object, which prevents Prisma's @updatedAt decorator from updating the updatedAt timestamp. This results in inaccurate cache status tracking, as the timestamp isn't updated when the cache is refreshed. To fix this, explicitly set the updatedAt field.

Throwing a generic Error for authentication failures results in a 500 response in tRPC. Instead, it should return a structured TRPCError with an appropriate code, such as FORBIDDEN, to accurately reflect the error type.
Date is formatted with hardcoded 'en-US' locale instead of using the user's locale from useLocale, which can lead to incorrect date representation for users in different locales.

false_positives.candidate:
Exclude expired cache rows from cache status

This status query groups every row for the credential without filtering `expiresAt`. Expired rows are ignored by `getCachedAvailability`, but remain in the database, so they can cause the UI to show a last-updated timestamp and a delete action even when no cache entry can be served. Filter to unexpired rows if this status is meant to represent usable cached data.

Invalidate the connected-calendar query after deleting cache

The delete mutation does not invalidate `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`; it only calls the optional `onSuccess` prop, which may be undefined. After deletion, the cached query can continue returning the old `cacheUpdatedAt`, so the dropdown still reports cache data and offers deletion until the query is otherwise refreshed. Invalidate the query on successful deletion (or ensure the callback always refreshes it).

Resolve the env file path independently of the caller's working directory

`ENV_FILE` is relative to the current working directory, not this script's location. Running the script from the repository root (for example, `./scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh`) reads or creates `../.env` instead of the repository's `.env`, so the app does not receive the configured webhook URL. Resolve the path from the script directory or set it explicitly.

true_positives.golden_comment: When immediateDelete is true, the deleteScheduledEmailReminder function cancels the SendGrid email but fails to delete the corresponding WorkflowReminder record from the database. This creates orphaned database entries and is inconsistent with the immediateDelete: false path, which marks the record as cancelled. The SendGrid DELETE API call is also omitted in this path.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Immediate cancellation bypasses the deferred-cancellation limit fix

This branch sends the SendGrid cancellation request immediately and returns without setting `cancelled` or deleting the reminder. It is used for rescheduling and workflow/step deletion, so cancellations for reminders scheduled far in the future accumulate in SendGrid's pending-cancellation list until their scheduled dates. That recreates the 100-pending-cancellations limit this change is intended to avoid; once the limit is reached, later cancellations can fail and the reminder emails can still be sent. The retained reminder rows also remain unmarked and are not picked up by the cancellation cron.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Asynchronous functions deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder are called without await inside forEach loops. This occurs during booking rescheduling/cancellation, and workflow/workflow step deletion/updates. Consequently, scheduled workflow reminders may not be reliably cancelled, potentially leaving them active.

The 'cancelled' field is nullable, which can lead to existing records having null values instead of a default of false. This can cause incorrect behavior in the application when checking the cancellation status of reminders.

false_positives.candidate:
The scheduler can schedule reminders already marked cancelled

This query selects unscheduled email reminders without excluding `cancelled: true`. A cancelled reminder whose scheduled date is more than an hour away is therefore submitted to SendGrid and marked scheduled, despite the cancellation marker. The cancellation cron may eventually cancel it near its scheduled date, but until then the supposedly cancelled email has been re-enqueued and can still be delivered if that later cancellation fails or does not run.

true_positives.golden_comment: The code uses forEach with async callbacks, which causes asynchronous operations (e.g., calendar/video event deletions, payment refunds) to run concurrently without being awaited. This 'fire-and-forget' behavior leads to unhandled promise rejections, race conditions, and incomplete cleanup, as surrounding try-catch blocks cannot properly handle errors from these unawaited promises. Replace forEach with for...of loops or Promise.all() with map() to ensure proper sequential execution and error handling.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Calendar and video cancellation is not awaited

The async callbacks passed to `forEach` are not awaited or collected. Since resolving the calendar now requires an asynchronous import, this function can send the reschedule email and return before calendar/video cancellations run; import or cancellation failures also escape the surrounding `try/catch`. A cancelled booking can therefore remain on an external calendar or retain its video meeting.

true_positives.golden_comment: Consider adding try-catch around the await to handle import failures gracefully

The async callbacks passed to `forEach` are not awaited or collected. Since resolving the calendar now requires an asynchronous import, this function can send the reschedule email and return before calendar/video cancellations run; import or cancellation failures also escape the surrounding `try/catch`. A cancelled booking can therefore remain on an external calendar or retain its video meeting.

false_positives.candidate:
All app imports are still started eagerly

Each `import()` is evaluated while this object is initialized, so importing `app-store` immediately starts loading every app module rather than loading an app only when its entry is used. This defeats the intended lazy-loading benefit and keeps startup work and module loading for unused integrations.

Reschedule mutation does not wait for integration cancellations

The async callbacks passed to `forEach` are not awaited or collected. With `getCalendar` now awaiting a dynamic import, the mutation can proceed to send its email and return before calendar or video cancellation has started or completed. This can leave the old booking active in an external calendar or video service after the reschedule is reported as successful.

true_positives.golden_comment: Incorrect end time calculation using slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Override validation allows slots extending past the override

This rejects a slot only when it ends before the override starts or starts after the override ends. A slot that starts inside the override but ends after it is accepted, as is one starting exactly at the override end. For example, a 60-minute slot starting at 10:30 passes a 10:00–11:00 override. This can advertise times when a fixed host is unavailable.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Using === for dayjs object comparison will always return false as it compares object references, not values. Use .isSame() method instead: dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').isSame(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, minutes))

false_positives.candidate:
Date overrides bypass booking and calendar conflicts

When a slot falls within a date override, this returns `true` before checking `busy`. Date overrides should replace the user's normal working hours, not make an already-booked or calendar-busy slot bookable. For fixed hosts in round-robin events, this can expose conflicting slots and allow double-bookings.

Split working hours incorrectly reject valid slots

The `.find()` rejects a slot if it is outside *any* working-hours interval on that day. With separate intervals such as 09:00–12:00 and 13:00–17:00, a 14:00 slot is rejected because it is outside the first interval, even though it fits the second. Check whether the slot fits at least one interval instead; otherwise users with split schedules lose valid availability.

true_positives.golden_comment: The code attempts to access integration.metadata[sender][login] without checking for the existence of the sender key. This causes a KeyError for integrations where the sender metadata was not set during creation
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Missing sender metadata raises instead of handling the installation

This lookup assumes every existing integration has `metadata['sender']['login']`, but `build_integration` only adds `sender` when the pipeline state contains it. If an existing integration has no organization integration and lacks that optional metadata, retrying setup raises `KeyError` and returns an error instead of completing or showing the intended installation failure.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Null reference if github_authenticated_user state is missing
OAuth state uses pipeline.signature (static) instead of a per-request random value

false_positives.candidate:
Skip installer identity validation when the webhook has not created the integration yet

When no `Integration` row exists for this installation, this branch advances the pipeline without comparing `github_authenticated_user` to the installation sender. A delayed or missing installation webhook therefore lets the OAuth-authenticated user complete setup for an installation created by a different GitHub user, bypassing the identity check this change is meant to enforce.

true_positives.golden_comment: The AssignmentSource dataclass uses queued: datetime = timezone.now() as a default field value, which evaluates timezone.now() once at class definition time and shares that single datetime instance across all objects.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
`queued` is fixed at module import time

`timezone.now()` is evaluated once when this module is imported, so every `AssignmentSource` created without an explicit `queued` value gets the same timestamp rather than its own creation time. Since `to_dict()` serializes this field, the recorded queue time is inaccurate for all later assignments. Use a `default_factory` so the timestamp is generated per instance.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The method name has a typo: test_from_dict_inalid_data should be test_from_dict_invalid_data.
Method name says 'empty_array' but tests empty dict - consider renaming to 'test_from_dict_empty_dict' for clarity.
to_dict() returns a datetime for queued; if this dict is passed in task kwargs (e.g., via apply_async), JSON serialization may fail depending on the serializer, which can cause enqueue errors.

true_positives.golden_comment: MetricAlertDetectorHandler inherits from StatefulDetectorHandler but only contains pass, failing to implement its required abstract methods: counter_names (property), get_dedupe_value(), get_group_key_values(), and build_occurrence_and_event_data(). This will cause a TypeError at runtime when the class is instantiated.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Registered metric alert handler is now abstract and cannot be instantiated

`MetricAlertDetectorHandler` inherits `StatefulDetectorHandler` but implements none of its abstract methods, including `counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, and the new occurrence hook. When a detector with this registered group type accesses `detector_handler`, instantiation raises `TypeError` instead of returning a handler, so processing that detector fails.

true_positives.golden_comment: Docstring says this returns a list of DetectorEvaluationResult, but the method now returns a dict keyed by DetectorGroupKey. Consider updating the docstring to match the new return type.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Evaluation docstring still describes a list return value

This method now returns a dictionary keyed by group key, but its docstring says it returns a list of `DetectorEvaluationResult`. That contradicts the method's contract and can mislead callers implementing or debugging detector handlers.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Wrong value `6` passed for `group_2` occurrence — the data packet specifies `"group_2": 10`. Should be `10` to accurately reflect the test scenario, which will ensure the test produces the correct occurrence data.
The function modifies the config variable to include display values but then returns the original monitor.config instead of the modified version.
The code fetches MonitorCheckIn objects by ID when the required data already exists in previous_checkins. This creates an unnecessary database query.

true_positives.golden_comment: Breaking out of the loop when the deadline has elapsed can skip terminating remaining flusher processes, potentially leaving them running after shutdown; consider ensuring termination is attempted even if the deadline is exceeded.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Timeout can leave later flusher processes running

When the join deadline expires while waiting for one process, this `break` skips every remaining process, including the `terminate()` call for those processes. They can continue flushing Redis segments and producing to Kafka after the strategy has shut down. Ensure every process is stopped even when the deadline is exhausted.

false_negatives.golden_comment: In the SpanFlusher flush loop, metric tags inconsistently use 'shard' (e.g., in spans.buffer.flusher.produce and spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes) and 'shards' (in spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce) for the same shard identifier value. This prevents correct metric aggregation across flush stages — dashboards and alerts filtering by tag 'shard' will miss data tagged as 'shards' and vice versa.
The test_basic function in test_consumer.py uses a monkeypatched time.sleep that returns immediately, but then calls time.sleep(0.1) expecting it to actually wait.

Because flusher processes are created via multiprocessing.get_context('spawn').Process, they are instances of multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess, which on POSIX is not a subclass of multiprocessing.Process, so this isinstance check will always be false and hung processes won't be killed here.
Sleep in test_consumer.py won’t actually wait because time.sleep was monkeypatched above; consider restoring sleep or using a different sync to ensure the flusher has time to process.

false_positives.candidate:
A negative process limit silently disables all flushers

The `--flusher-processes` option accepts negative integers, and a negative `max_processes` makes `num_processes` negative. The subsequent `range(self.num_processes)` creates no worker processes, so segments are never flushed to Kafka and can accumulate in Redis. Reject non-positive limits or otherwise ensure at least one worker is created.

Inserting this parameter breaks positional callers

`produce_to_pipe` was previously the third positional argument to `SpanFlusher`; inserting `max_processes` before it means existing calls such as `SpanFlusher(buffer, next_step, callback)` now treat the callback as a process limit. Initialization then attempts to use that callback in `min()` and fails. Preserve the existing positional argument order, for example by adding the new parameter after `produce_to_pipe`.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The magic number 50 for max_wait is used repeatedly throughout the tests. Consider extracting this as a named constant to improve maintainability.
The test test_thread_queue_parallel_error_handling has a docstring that doesn't match the test implementation.

false_positives.candidate:
A negative worker count creates a zero-queue pool

`max_workers` is passed directly as `num_queues` when it is negative. The pool then creates no queues, and processing a message fails during `hash(group_key) % self.num_queues`; `submit` catches that error and marks the message's offset complete, allowing it to be committed without processing. Validate that the configured worker count is positive before starting the consumer.

Closing one strategy permanently shuts down the shared worker pool

The queue pool is created once on `ResultsStrategyFactory` and reused by every strategy returned from `create_with_partitions`, but closing any one strategy shuts that shared pool down. Arroyo can create and close strategies again when partitions are reassigned; the replacement strategy then submits to queues whose workers have exited (or which reject submissions), so processing stops after a rebalance.

Failed result processing is still marked complete

The `finally` block marks every work item complete, including items whose processor raised an exception. `ResultProcessor.__call__` also catches and suppresses exceptions from `handle_result`, so those failures appear successful to this worker. The commit loop can therefore advance past a result that was never processed, preventing Kafka from replaying it and causing data loss.

Queues are unbounded and provide no backpressure

`queue.Queue()` defaults to `maxsize=0`, which means unlimited capacity. If messages arrive faster than workers process them, the consumer continues enqueueing work instead of slowing ingestion; queued payloads can grow until the process runs out of memory. This also contradicts the strategy's stated backpressure guarantee.

Unseen Kafka offsets can permanently block commits

This loop requires every integer offset between the first and last observed offsets to be present in `all_offsets`. Kafka consumers can legitimately observe gaps, for example from compacted records or transactional control records. When that happens, processing later messages will never make the missing offset appear, so commits remain stuck at the gap and the consumer can accumulate an unbounded backlog.

true_positives.golden_comment: The cache key construction in `userPermDenialCacheKey` uses simple string concatenation with underscores, which can lead to ambiguous keys and collision risks when any component contains underscores or is empty. This could result in incorrect denial cache hits, affecting user permissions.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Unescaped key components can collide

The key concatenates the resource name and parent folder with underscores, so different valid name/folder pairs can produce the same key (for example, name `a_b` with parent `c` and name `a` with parent `b_c`). A denial for one resource can then incorrectly deny access to the other until the entry expires. Encode or delimit components unambiguously.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The Check operation exhibits asymmetric cache trust logic: cached permission grants are trusted and returned immediately, but cached denials from the same permission cache are ignored, leading to a fresh database lookup. This allows stale cached grants to provide access to revoked resources, posing a security risk.
The test comment says the cached permissions 'allow access', but the map stores false for dashboards:uid:dash1, so checkPermission will still treat this scope as not allowed.

false_positives.candidate:
A cached denial can block newly granted access

This returns a prior denial without rechecking current permissions. If a user was denied for a resource before it was created or before access was granted, the same request continues to be denied for the cache TTL (30 seconds), even though the database now allows it. This can prevent the newly created dashboards or folders this change is intended to make accessible from loading immediately.

Denial cache key does not distinguish identity types

The key identifies a principal only by its UID, but checks also support distinct identity types such as users and service accounts. If those identity namespaces contain the same UID, a denial cached for one identity will incorrectly deny the other identity's request for the same resource and action. Include the identity type in the key.

true_positives.golden_comment: The rendered GrafanaRuleListItem is missing the required key prop for React list items. This can cause rendering issues when the list order changes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Filtered Grafana rules are rendered without stable React keys

The Grafana item returned from this `rules.map` omits the `key` that is already computed for each result. React therefore warns about missing keys and may reuse the wrong item component when results are reconciled, which can associate action state with a different rule.

true_positives.golden_comment: RuleActionsButtons is invoked with only promRule, but SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer inside RuleActionsButtons still depends on a Grafana Ruler rule being present, so for Grafana rules coming from list views the 'Silence notifications' menu entry (now driven by Grafana Prom abilities) will toggle showSilenceDrawer without ever rendering the drawer. Silence action does not open its drawer for Prometheus-only rules

The menu now derives silence permission from `promRule`, so it can display Silence for a Grafana rule loaded without a ruler rule. Clicking it sets `showSilenceDrawer`, but this condition requires `rule` to be a Grafana ruler alerting rule; in the new list path `rule` is absent, so the drawer never renders and the menu action does nothing.

false_positives.candidate:
Grafana list rules lose Pause and Delete actions

This new list item passes only `promRule` to the action buttons, so `AlertRuleMenu` receives no `rulerRule`. false_negatives.golden_comment: The applyTemplateVariables method is called with request.filters as the third parameter, but this parameter is not used in the corresponding test setup.

false_positives.candidate:
Preserve range-variable detection before interpolation

`querySupportsSplitting` runs after this interpolation and relies on `isQueryWithRangeVariable` to keep `$__range` queries unsplit. If `applyTemplateVariables` expands `$__range` using the original request range, that check no longer sees the token and the query is split; each subrequest then uses a fixed full-range duration instead of the range for that subrequest. This produces incorrect results. Preserve the original expression for the splitting check, or otherwise keep range-variable queries unsplit.

Shard queries are interpolated twice

Shard splitting interpolates each target here, then passes it to `runSplitQuery`, which now calls `applyTemplateVariables` again before execution. The second pass can expand variable-like text introduced by the first interpolation—for example, a variable value containing `$name` or a Grafana macro—changing the query unexpectedly. Avoid re-interpolating already-prepared shard targets, or ensure interpolation happens only once.

true_positives.golden_comment: Race condition: Multiple concurrent requests could pass the device count check simultaneously and create devices beyond the limit. Consider using a database transaction or lock.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
The count-then-insert check can exceed the configured limit

The device count and subsequent insert run as separate database operations with no transaction or serialization. If the count is one below the limit, concurrent requests for different devices can both observe that count and both insert, exceeding the configured limit. Enforce the check and insert atomically (or otherwise serialize limit decisions) so concurrent requests cannot overrun it.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `tagDeviceUI` function populates the local cache with the device ID before the `CreateOrUpdateDevice` call. true_positives.matched_candidate:
A rejected device is cached, so its next request bypasses the limit

`tagDeviceUI` inserts the device ID into the local cache before attempting the store write. When the store rejects a new device at the limit, this error is now returned here, but the cache entry is not removed. A retry from that device hits the cache and returns success without checking the limit, so the user authenticates anonymously for the cache lifetime without being recorded. Remove the cache entry when the store write fails, or only cache successful writes.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Anonymous authentication now fails entirely if anonDeviceService.TagDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached. Previously, device tagging was asynchronous and non-blocking. This change prevents anonymous users from authenticating when the device limit is reached.

true_positives.golden_comment: The code uses Error log level for what appears to be debugging information. This will pollute error logs in production. Consider using Debug or Info level instead.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Successful cleanup batches are logged as errors

This logs at error level unconditionally, including when `err` is nil and when the query finds no IDs. Normal cleanup cycles will therefore produce error-level log entries (and include potentially large ID lists), creating misleading alerts and unnecessary log volume. The other new cleanup batch logs at lines 537, 554, 557, 576, and 579 have the same issue.

true_positives.golden_comment: The cleanup job ticker was changed from 10 minutes to 1 minute, which can lead to increased database load and contention due to more frequent execution of cleanup tasks. This change should be reviewed to ensure it aligns with performance expectations.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Cleanup now runs ten times as often

This changes the global cleanup scheduler from every 10 minutes to every minute, although the PR only addresses annotation cleanup. Every cleanup job—not just annotation cleanup—will therefore run much more frequently, increasing database and filesystem load; if a run takes longer than a minute, a queued tick can also trigger another run immediately afterward.

false_positives.candidate:
Building the inline ID list has quadratic cost

Each iteration formats a new string containing the entire accumulated ID list. For a configured batch of N IDs, this repeatedly copies the growing string, giving quadratic allocation and CPU cost. Large batches take this SQLite path (the new test configures 32,767), so cleanup can incur substantial avoidable work; build the list with a builder or join instead.

true_positives.golden_comment: In DualWriterMode3's DeleteCollection method, when a storage operation fails, recordStorageDuration is incorrectly called with recordLegacyDuration instead.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Legacy delete-collection duration is recorded as a storage operation

This goroutine measures the legacy `DeleteCollection` call but records it with `recordStorageDuration`, so legacy latency and errors are attributed to unified storage and the legacy metrics omit this operation. Use the legacy duration recorder; otherwise monitoring cannot accurately show whether the asynchronous legacy write is succeeding or slowing down.

true_positives.golden_comment: Inconsistency: using name instead of options.Kind for metrics recording differs from other methods.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Delete metric uses the resource name as the kind label

This call passes `name` where the other storage-duration calls pass `options.Kind`. If that argument is the metric's kind label, every distinct deleted object name creates a separate label value, causing unbounded Prometheus cardinality and making the metric inconsistent with other operations. Pass the resource kind instead.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The context is being created with d.Log instead of the log variable that was initialized with additional context values (name, kind, method). This means those values won't be propagated to the logging context.

false_positives.candidate:
Async legacy writes inherit the request context

The timeout context is derived from the incoming request context, which is normally canceled when the handler returns. Since the legacy operation runs after the method returns, it can receive an already-canceled context and abort instead of writing. The same pattern is used for update, delete, and delete-collection, so mode 3 can leave legacy storage stale despite successful unified writes.

true_positives.golden_comment: The GetWebAssets function implements an incomplete double-checked locking pattern for caching web assets. The function first checks if the cache is populated using a read lock (RLock), and if the cache is empty, it acquires a write lock to populate it. However, it fails to re-check whether the cache was populated by another goroutine while waiting to acquire the write lock.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Recheck the cache after acquiring the write lock

Concurrent callers can all observe a nil cache before this lock, then wait here. Once the first caller loads and stores the assets, each waiting caller still proceeds to load and overwrite the cache because the cached value is never checked again. This causes redundant serialized I/O and, if callers have different configs, can return and leave cached assets from a different config than the one that initialized the cache. Recheck the cache under the lock for non-dev callers before loading.

false_negatives.golden_comment: In addition to the missing double-check, the function has a critical flaw in its error handling: it unconditionally assigns the fetch result to the cache (line 69: entryPointAssetsCache = result) regardless of whether the fetch succeeded or failed. When an error occurs during asset fetching, result is nil, and this nil value overwrites any previously valid cache entry.
The enableSqlExpressions function has flawed logic that always returns false, effectively disabling SQL expressions unconditionally:
The DB methods NewInMemoryDB().RunCommands, DB.QueryFramesInto, and DB.TablesList in pkg/expr/sql/db.go return hardcoded 'not implemented' errors after removing the go-duck dependency.

true_positives.golden_comment: A race condition in BuildIndex allows multiple goroutines to concurrently build the same expensive index for the same key. This is caused by moving the b.cacheMu lock from protecting the entire function to only protecting the final cache assignment.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Concurrent builds can open the same Bleve index

The build-wide lock has been removed, but `getOrCreateIndex` can still have multiple callers observe a cache miss for the same key and call `BuildIndex` concurrently. For file-backed indexes, both builds use the same directory, so concurrent `bleve.New` calls can fail or interfere; even if both complete, whichever stores last replaces the cached index. Serialize builds per key or recheck the cache before creating the index.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Calling s.search.TotalDocs() here may race with concurrent index creation: TotalDocs iterates b.cache without synchronization, and the event watcher goroutine started just above could trigger BuildIndex writes concurrently, potentially causing a concurrent map read/write panic.

false_positives.candidate:
Startup indexing races on shared state

Calling `Init` during construction runs `searchSupport.init` immediately, where multiple errgroup workers concurrently increment `totalBatchesIndexed` and assign to the shared `err` variable. This is a data race, and concurrent error assignments can cause initialization to return the wrong result. Use per-worker local errors and an atomic or synchronized counter before enabling parallel startup indexing.

true_positives.golden_comment: Cleanup reference uses incorrect alias - should be 'idp-alias-' + i instead of 'alias'.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Cleanup targets the literal alias `alias`

This registers cleanup against `identityProviders().get("alias")`, not the IDP created in the loop. The cleanup therefore leaves all generated `idp-alias-*` providers behind (and the later cleanup registration at line 425 has the same problem). The test can contaminate the shared test realm and fail on reruns or affect other tests.

false_negatives.golden_comment: InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin() recursively calls session.identityProviders().getById() instead of idpDelegate.getById(), causing the cache lookup to re-enter the same caching layer.

true_positives.golden_comment: Abstract order() method on CryptoProvider may break backward compatibility with existing implementations
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Adding an abstract SPI method breaks existing CryptoProvider implementations

`CryptoProvider` is a public service-provider interface, and making `order()` abstract breaks source compatibility for every existing third-party implementation. More importantly, an older implementation can still be discovered at runtime, but the new sorting code invokes `order()` on it and gets `AbstractMethodError`, preventing crypto-provider initialization. Give the method a default priority to preserve compatibility, or otherwise provide a migration path that does not fail during discovery.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Returns wrong provider (default keystore instead of BouncyCastle)

Dead code exists where ASN1Encoder instances are created and written to, but their results are immediately discarded. The actual encoding is performed by new ASN1Encoder instances created in the subsequent return statement, rendering the earlier operations useless.
When length starts at -1 from indefinite-length encoding, the arithmetic 'length = length - bytes.length' will behave unexpectedly, potentially leading to incorrect processing of encoded data.

false_positives.candidate:
Equal-priority providers leave FIPS selection dependent on discovery order

The built-in `DefaultCryptoProvider`, `WildFlyElytronProvider`, and `FIPS1402Provider` all return priority 200. The comparator therefore does not distinguish them, and the stable sort preserves ServiceLoader enumeration order; when multiple providers are present, whichever is discovered first is selected, with no guarantee that the FIPS provider wins. A classpath containing both FIPS and non-FIPS providers can consequently initialize with non-FIPS cryptography despite the FIPS provider being available. Assign distinct priorities or reject ambiguous top-priority providers.

true_positives.golden_comment: In hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope), the resource lookup uses findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId()), but AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource creates per-client resources with the owner set to resourceServer.getClientId(), so this lookup will never find those resources and will always fall back to the 'all-clients' resource, effectively ignoring client-specific permissions.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Resource lookups use the resource-server ID as the owner

The third argument to `findByName` filters by resource owner, but schema-created resources are owned by `resourceServer.getClientId()` (see `AdminPermissionsSchema`). Passing `server.getId()` here means client-specific resources are not found; the equivalent lookup at line 244 also misses the all-clients resource. Consequently, V2 client permission checks cannot find their resources and authorized administrators are denied.

The AdminPermissions event listener, responsible for cleaning up permissions upon role, client, or group removal, is incorrectly guarded by the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) feature flag. Consequently, if ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled but V1 is not, the permission cleanup logic will not execute, leading to orphaned permission data.
